sentences.text: 1 .  We have heard Ms. Kharkar, learned counsel for the petitioners and Dr. Birendra Saraf, learned Advocate General on the backdrop of earlier orders 08 August, 2024 5-WP 6330-21@IA 10095-24@WP 3394-19.DOC passed by us.

sentences.text: 2. sentences.text:

sentences.text: Dr. Saraf has submitted that as observed by this Court in the previous orders, a decision has been taken and the State Government is in the process of issuing a notification declaring two additional authorities, i.e., for Amravati and Nashik Division.

sentences.text: He states that Nashik authority would also be having jurisdiction in regard to Pune and Konkan Division and Amravati Divisional Authority in respect of Amravati, Akola, Buldhana, Yawatmal and Washim.

sentences.text:

5.
sentences._hearing_file: Rajendra Nivrutti Zurange And Ors vs The Union Of India And Ors on 8 August, 2024.json

sentences.text: We are of the opinion that let such notification, which is in the process of being issued, be placed on record on the adjourned date of hearing.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners, however, submits that pendency of the proceedings before Konkan, Pune and Nashik Division is quite large, as also it may not be convenient for the litigants of Konkan to travel all the way to Nashik, as also the litigants from Pune Division to Nashik in regard to adjudication of their cases as already meager amount of compensation is being paid.

sentences.text: It is submitted that this would be causing prejudice to large number of litigants to travel all the way to Nashik for adjudication of their reference proceedings.

sentences.text:

opennyai_summary.17_January_2023__decision:
We have requested for intervention to the learned Advocate General to take steps to appoint member of competent authorities and shall make an endeavor to appoint one authority in every district, at the earliest.
Steps shall be taken for appointment of competent authority immediately where there are more number of matters pending under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
It is made clear that since there is no appointment of competent authority in other districts and whose maters are to be heard by competent authority at Aurangabad, competent authority at Aurangabad is requested not to impose any cost upon the claimants while seeking adjournment, in future.
opennyai_summary.17_January_2023__facts: We are informed that the competent authority having jurisdiction in Aurangabad before whom the matters of certain revenue district are referred, in view there being no separate competent authority for the districts, are imposing costs against the parties from revenue district taking adjournment.

opennyai_summary.20_February_2023__facts:
Learned Advocate General for the State Government states that the Competent Authority is already appointed at Aurangabad for hearing the reference under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
We direct the State Government to set up the Competent Authority at Amravati Division and Nashik Division within eight weeks from today, without fail.
The Competent Authority would be appointed for Nashik Division and would be directed to hold circuit hearings at Konkan Division and Pune Division depending upon the number of references pending before the Konkan Division as well as 3-wp6330-21c.doc Pune Division.
opennyai_summary.20_February_2023__arguments: 5. Mr.Kapse, learned counsel for High Court made a suggestion that instead of giving two months time to the State Government to set up the Competent Authority at Amravati Division and Nashik Division, less time should be granted, in any event before 31st March, 2023 with a view that the budget earmarked for the financial year 2022-2023 is available for setting up of the two posts of the Competent Authority and if the time is granted beyond 31st March, 2023, budget otherwise available for the financial year 2022-2023 shall get lapsed and, in that event, the State Government would not be able to appoint the Competent Authority in view of the funds not being available earmarked in budget for 2023-24.
opennyai_summary.20_February_2023__decision:
6. We have granted eight weeks time with a mandatory direction to the State Government to appoint the Competent Authority so as to obviate the request for extension of time after expiry of six weeks.
It is made clear that the State Government shall earmark funds in the budget for the financial year 2023-2024, if required and for setting up a Competent Authority for Pune and other Divisions so that there would not be any impediment for the purpose of setting up of the Competent Authority within eight weeks.
The 3-wp6330-21c.doc State Government would provide budgetary provision for setting up of the Competent Authority in future if any decision is taken by the State Government on its own or if directed by this Court to the State Government.
7. We accept the assurance given by the learned Advocate General that the Competent Authority would be set up as directed above within the time prescribed so as to mitigate the hardship caused to the litigants, whose references are pending and would be filed.
8. Place both the Writ Petitions on board under the caption of directions for reporting compliance on 2nd May, 2023.

opennyai_summary.issue: 2. The issue in the present proceedings concerns the State Government taking appropriate steps to notify the Maharashtra Land Acquisition and Settlement Authority in terms of Section 51 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Act, 2013.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
Dr. Saraf has submitted that as observed by this Court in the previous orders, a decision has been taken and the State Government is in the process of issuing a notification declaring two additional authorities, i.e., for Amravati and Nashik Division.
It is submitted that this would be causing prejudice to large number of litigants to travel all the way to Nashik for adjudication of their reference proceedings.
